title: spec review: S2 v3: execution waves in daemon.dispatch behind [scheduler].mode = shadow|active|off — interference-compatible wave logged to runs/sched/waves.jsonl, applied only in active mode (spec reviews T-0523 and T-0525 folded in)
spec:
Goal T-0503, brief .orchestrator/adaptive-parallelism-program.md section P3 (select the best set of mutually compatible ready tasks; respect depends_on, capacity, budgets, cooldowns, safety policy) and Evaluation (retain what baseline scheduling would have done). Base goal/T-0503 with S0a (schedlog, dispatch.jsonl considered rows with a capacity_reason local of cooldown|account_capacity|executor_capacity, first_ready_at) and S1 (interference.select_wave, pairwise, classify with a transitive _depends_on walk over the tasks dict) merged. Work only in your worktree, commit only on your own branch with the task id in the message, run the full .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh before reporting; report sha and failures only. Tests are unittest.TestCase methods.
Facts: daemon.dispatch walks bus.read(status="queued", role="execute") + retry_held (budget-held tasks with no dispatched_at) in id order and dispatches first-come until free_slots; _load_review_cfg(pool) (daemon.py:217) shows the pool.toml table pattern but is called only from tick(), while the Daemon tests call daemon.dispatch(pool) directly. interference.select_wave(ready, running, tasks, capacity, order=None, graph=None, rules=None) -> {wave, deferred} takes and returns task ids; interference.pairwise(tasks_list) takes task dicts.
1. _load_scheduler_cfg(pool): table [scheduler] with defaults mode = "shadow" (off|shadow|active), soft_conflict_policy = "defer", max_wave = 0 (0 = capacity); called at the top of dispatch(pool) itself so tests calling dispatch directly observe the mode. Add the table to .orchestrator/pool.toml with comments (default shadow: dispatch unchanged, waves only logged; active dispatches the wave; off disables both); touch install.py only if pool.toml is templated there.
2. Extract the existing per-task eligibility into one side-effect-free helper _first_come_order(pool, candidates, slots) -> ordered ids that would dispatch this tick under the current rules (ready, non-stale, spec approved or below SPEC_REVIEW_MIN, fallback tier available in fallback mode, slot decrement); both the real off/shadow dispatch path and baseline_order call it, so the two orderings cannot diverge. Candidates = queued execute tasks plus the budget-held retries from retry_held (their held status is irrelevant to selection).
3. Once per tick: running = execute tasks with status running plus dispatched-but-unclaimed ones; tasks = dict id -> task covering candidates, running, their goal siblings and the full transitive depends_on ancestry of every candidate and running task (walk depends_on through bus.get; missing ids are skipped, never raise). order = _wave_order(candidate_ids, tasks), a module-level hook returning its input unchanged (a later task replaces it). result = interference.select_wave(candidate_ids, running_ids, tasks, capacity=min(slots, max_wave or slots), order=order, rules={"soft_conflict_policy": ...}). predicted = interference.pairwise([tasks[i] for i in result["wave"]]). When mode != off and candidates exist: schedlog.append("waves", {"ts","mode","ready": candidate_ids,"running": running_ids,"baseline_order": _first_come_order(...),"wave","deferred","predicted","priority": {},"applied": mode == "active"}).
4. mode off or shadow: dispatch exactly as before. mode active: dispatch the wave in wave order and no other task this tick; each deferred candidate is recorded in the dispatch.jsonl considered row as skipped with reason "predicted_interference" for hard or soft deferrals and the existing capacity_reason value (cooldown|account_capacity|executor_capacity) for capacity deferrals. Invariants in every mode: never more dispatches than slots; never a task whose dependencies are not merged; never a hard-conflicting pair co-dispatched in active mode; spec-review creation and the review respawn loop unchanged.
5. README Pipeline section: one paragraph on [scheduler] modes and the waves log.
6. Tests in tests/test_daemon.py: ::test_scheduler_cfg_defaults, ::test_dispatch_shadow_logs_wave_and_keeps_first_come, ::test_dispatch_active_defers_hard_conflict_with_running_task, ::test_dispatch_active_respects_slots_and_dependencies, ::test_dispatch_mode_off_writes_no_wave_rows, ::test_dispatch_wave_includes_budget_retry_candidates, ::test_dispatch_active_capacity_deferral_keeps_capacity_reason, ::test_wave_tasks_cover_cross_goal_dependency_ancestry. Existing tests stay green.
acceptance: tests/test_daemon.py::test_scheduler_cfg_defaults and tests/test_daemon.py::test_dispatch_shadow_logs_wave_and_keeps_first_come pass: [scheduler] mode defaults to shadow, dispatch order and set are unchanged, and every tick with candidates appends a waves.jsonl row with ready, running, baseline_order (from the shared _first_come_order helper), wave, deferred, predicted and applied false

tests/test_daemon.py::test_dispatch_active_defers_hard_conflict_with_running_task, tests/test_daemon.py::test_dispatch_active_respects_slots_and_dependencies and tests/test_daemon.py::test_dispatch_active_capacity_deferral_keeps_capacity_reason pass: mode active dispatches only the selected wave, never a hard-conflicting pair together, never beyond free slots or unmet dependencies, and records deferred candidates in dispatch.jsonl as predicted_interference or the existing capacity_reason
full .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh exits 0 and the suite gains eight tests

risks.issue: Point 3 never defines what `candidate_ids` (the `ready` argument passed to interference.select_wave) actually is. select_wave's own contract expects the FULL eligible, uncapped-by-slots set so it can backfill a slot freed by a hard/soft deferral with a later clean candidate (that's the whole value of 'select the best set of mutually compatible ready tasks' from the P3 brief). If an implementer instead feeds it the slots-capped output of `_first_come_order`/`baseline_order` (the only concretely-specified helper), a deferred conflict just shrinks the wave below capacity instead of being backfilled, and none of the eight named tests (capacity/dependency/hard-conflict-with-running/budget-retry/cross-goal-ancestry) would catch it.

Point 3 requires the `tasks` dict to also cover 'their goal siblings' for every candidate/running task, but select_wave/pairwise only ever compare candidate_ids ∪ running_ids against each other, and the transitive depends_on walk already resolves any id it encounters on demand via bus.get regardless of goal membership. As scoped, including goal siblings has no observable effect on wave/deferred/predicted output, so no listed test can verify it was implemented (or omitted) correctly -- it's either dead requirement or under-specified (if it's meant to feed something not otherwise described).

_load_scheduler_cfg is specified to default mode to "shadow" but the spec never asks it to validate the value against off|shadow|active, unlike _load_review_cfg's code_review handling (daemon.py:230-237) which notifies once and falls back to a safe default on an unrecognised value. A typo'd pool.toml mode would silently take whichever branch the mode=="active"/mode!="off" comparisons happen to fall into instead of being surfaced.

suggested_spec_changes: Explicitly define candidate_ids as the full eligibility-filtered ready set (ready, non-stale, spec-approved-or-below-spec_review_min, fallback-tier-available) with NO slot cap -- distinct from baseline_order/_first_come_order's slots-capped output -- so select_wave can backfill a deferred slot from a later candidate.
Add a ninth test asserting backfill: capacity 2, three ready candidates where A hard-conflicts with a running task and B/C are clean; assert mode active dispatches [B, C], not just [B].

Either drop 'their goal siblings' from the tasks-dict requirement in point 3 or state the concrete mechanism that needs it, since select_wave/pairwise never compare against tasks outside candidate_ids ∪ running_ids and the depends_on walk resolves ids on demand.
Have _load_scheduler_cfg validate [scheduler].mode against off|shadow|active with the same notify-once-and-fallback-to-shadow pattern _load_review_cfg uses for code_review.
